chunks: And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever recites Surah Al-Ilaf (Quraish) frequently, Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment on a mount from the mounts of Paradise until he sits at the tables of light on the Day of Judgment.

The compiler of this book (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Whoever recites Surah Al-Feel, let him recite Al-Ilaf with it in a single rak'ah of an obligatory prayer, for they are both one Surah, and it is not permissible to recite only one of them alone.

key_terms.إِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ: Surah Quraish (also referred to as Al-Ilaf)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Surah Al-Feel and Surah Quraish together in prayer?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, Surah Al-Ilaf (Quraish) is often viewed as the first Meccan Surah, establishing the divine favor of Quraysh's safety and trade, which this hadith links to a reward of seating at 'tables of light'—a metaphor for elevated spiritual proximity. The compiler, Shaykh al-Saduq, provides a specific juristic nuance that these two short Surahs form a single unit in obligatory prayer, emphasizing their thematic unity in recounting Allah's protection of the Holy Sanctuary.
